A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Thera research. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and can be matched despite extensive restructuring and revised experiments.

before.justification: v2 reports original super-resolution PSNR/SSIM results, ablations, multi-scale consistency measurements and computational-resource comparisons.

after.justification: v3 reports original super-resolution results and ablations, a derivative-fidelity comparison, and new COZ optical-zoom results for Thera++.

M1.justification: Thera-S and Thera-L are retained as Air and Plus, while Thera-M is dropped. v3 adds the transformer-based Pro hypernetwork and Thera++, which augments Plus with an STN predicting a six-parameter affine transform (Appendices D–E). The underlying thermal field, TV regularizer and standard inference construction remain.

E1.justification: v3 adds training and testing on COZ real optical-zoom data (Appendix E/Table 6), extending the work beyond synthetic downsampling to actual imaging conditions with alignment errors and scene changes. DIV2K and the five conventional benchmark datasets remain.

E2.justification: SRNO and MSIT join the DIV2K and standard-benchmark comparisons. They also replace LTE and CiaoSR in the main qualitative comparison. The new COZ comparison includes LMI; its LIT[9] row cites the existing CLIT work.

E3.justification: SwinIR backbone evaluations are removed, standard-benchmark and SSIM tables switch to RDN, and ablations switch from Thera-M to Plus. SSIM evaluation is shortened from scales through ×30 to ×8, and benchmark ×12 evaluations disappear. v3 also specifies DIV2K-only MSIT retraining in two 1050-epoch stages. The main Thera patch-sampling, optimizer, training-budget and self-ensemble recipe remains unchanged.

E4.justification: The quantitative multi-scale consistency study in v2 Section 4.2/Table 3 is removed. v3 adds the LIIF-versus-Thera signal/derivative diagnostic in Figure 5 and reports the existing design ablations for Plus instead of M, including a changed finding about predicted frequency components (Table 3).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The discussion of variance across methods is not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds Pro results, including 35.19 dB for EDSR ×2, and revises retained entries, such as L/Plus at EDSR ×2 from 34.88 to 34.89 dB. New COZ results include 29.06 dB for Thera++ versus 28.86 for LMI at ×2. Benchmark, SSIM and ablation results are substantially replaced under changed backbones/variants; SwinIR, consistency and resource-result entries are removed.

T1.justification: The thermal activation, heat-equation/Gaussian-PSF formulation, diffusivity derivation, t=S² relationship, TV definition and frequency-initialization law are retained in Section 3 and Appendix A. The neural-heat-field terminology, smoothness discussion and new illustrations do not introduce a new formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions—analytical Gaussian anti-aliasing and parameter-efficient arbitrary-scale super-resolution—remain. v2's qualified claim of outperforming competitors in most cases becomes a claim of outperforming all competing methods in v3's introduction and consistently outperforming them in its conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 explains the disadvantage of predicted frequencies as difficult joint learning; v3 instead reports negligible gains and justifies sharing by parameter cost. v3 adds derivative-fidelity and COZ misalignment interpretations, while removing the ×2 anisotropy explanation and the caution about small legacy benchmarks. The single-hidden-layer limitation remains, now qualified as sufficient for the tested subpixel range.

D1.justification: v3 adds Pro block/head specifications, Thera++ STN details, the TorchMetrics SSIM implementation and MSIT retraining instructions. It removes the hardware/timing/VRAM section and some ConvNeXt implementation specifics. Direct code/pretrained-model access information becomes a project-page link, and the separate single-image PyTorch implementation is no longer mentioned.

R1.justification: Related work adds SRNO, MSIT and BANF, with further citations for COZ/LMI, spatial transformers and supporting implementations. Some earlier technical references disappear. The basic positioning against learned, scale-conditioned observation models remains, with a more explicit critique of their fidelity and generalization.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten around neural heat fields. Related-work subsections are reordered; learning the SR prior, TV regularization and training receive separate subsections; and the appendices are reorganized with references moved after them. The title, author list and ASSR/ASR terminology also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from one-column to two-column layout, with redesigned overview diagrams and restructured tables. v3 adds derivative and PSF illustrations and an introductory parameter-performance plot, while revising existing plots to logarithmic parameter axes. The filtering example moves to the appendix; the detailed architecture schematic and extended qualitative grids are removed.

improvement.justification: v3 improves empirical relevance through the real optical-zoom test and newer comparator evaluations, including documented DIV2K-only MSIT retraining, and makes the observation-model explanation clearer. These gains provide a limited net improvement, tempered by removal of direct scale-consistency validation and runtime/VRAM evidence. The COZ results also concern an STN-augmented variant without isolating the STN contribution.
